name: Weak RCA: orders down with stable traffic, scattered guesses and no funnel

messages.text: At Zalando, weekly completed orders fell 15% week-on-week, but unique visitors and page views are flat. How would you approach this?
My first thought is a competitor is running a big sale, so people are looking on our site but buying somewhere else. That happens a lot in fashion.
Possibly. How would you check whether that's actually what's happening?
I'd look at competitor websites and see if they have sales on. Also maybe our prices went up, so I'd ask the pricing team.
Pricing hasn't changed, and marketing spend is the same as last month. Is there anything in our own data you'd look at?
Yeah, maybe the site is slow. Or people don't like the new products this season. I'd probably send a survey to users asking why they didn't buy.
A survey would take a while. Is there a faster way to see where shoppers are dropping off?
I guess we could look at the checkout. But honestly I still think it's the competitor thing, it's a really common reason.
Let's say we did look, and add-to-bag rates are normal but cart-to-checkout dropped sharply. What does that tell you?
That people are adding things and then leaving. So they're probably comparing prices with the competitor. We could send them a discount code for what's in their cart.
Okay. How would you wrap up?
I'd send discount emails to people with abandoned carts and maybe match the competitor's sale prices, and that should get orders back up.
